Dental Implants on Finance in London – 2026 Guide

Written By

Dental Implants Team

Dental implants are widely regarded as one of the most effective long-term solutions for replacing missing teeth. However, the cost of treatment can be a significant consideration for many patients. Understanding how dental implant finance works in London — and what options may be available — can help you plan your treatment with greater clarity and confidence.

This guide is designed to explain how dental implants London finance typically works, what patients should consider before applying, and how to approach payment planning responsibly. It is important to note that finance is always subject to status, lender approval and individual eligibility — approval is never guaranteed.

How Much Do Dental Implants Cost in London?

The cost of dental implants in London varies depending on a number of clinical factors. There is no single fixed price, because every patient’s oral health, bone condition and treatment needs are different.

What Factors Influence the Cost?

  • Number of implants required — replacing a single tooth is different in cost from replacing several teeth or a full arch
  • Bone grafting or sinus lift procedures — if bone volume is insufficient, preparatory procedures may be needed before implants can be placed
  • Type of restoration — whether a single crown, bridge or full-arch prosthesis is required
  • Complexity of the case — patients with gum disease, previous dental work or medical considerations may require additional planning
  • Material choices — the type of crown or prosthetic material used can affect the overall cost

Because of these variables, it is essential to receive a personalised assessment before any cost can be confirmed. A thorough consultation allows the dentist to evaluate your oral health, take any necessary scans and provide a written treatment plan with transparent pricing.

For more detail on what influences pricing, visit our page on dental implant costs in London.

Can You Pay for Dental Implants in Monthly Instalments?

Many dental practices in London offer the option to spread the cost of implant treatment over a series of monthly payments. This is typically arranged through a third-party finance provider and allows patients to manage the cost of treatment alongside their regular household budget.

How Does Dental Finance Typically Work?

  • You receive a treatment plan with the total cost of your proposed treatment
  • A finance application is submitted to a regulated lending partner
  • If approved, you agree to a fixed repayment schedule with clearly defined monthly payments
  • Treatment can usually begin once the finance agreement is in place

It is important to understand that finance applications involve a credit check and are subject to lender approval. Not all applications will be accepted, and the terms offered may vary depending on your individual financial circumstances. Monthly payment amounts depend on the total treatment cost, the deposit paid and the length of the repayment term.

What Does 0% Finance Mean for Dental Implants?

Some dental practices offer interest-free finance over shorter repayment periods — commonly 6 or 12 months. This means you pay back only the amount borrowed, with no additional interest charges.

Are There Longer-Term Finance Options?

Yes. For patients who need to spread the cost over a longer period, extended finance plans of 24, 36, 48 or 60 months may be available. These longer-term plans typically carry an interest charge (APR), which increases the total amount repayable. The specific rate offered depends on the lender and the applicant’s creditworthiness.

Responsible Borrowing Considerations

  • Always review the total amount repayable, not just the monthly figure
  • Understand whether the plan is interest-free or interest-bearing
  • Check whether early repayment is permitted without penalty
  • Ensure monthly repayments fit comfortably within your budget
  • Read the full finance agreement carefully before signing

Finance offers, where available, are subject to status and may not be offered to every applicant. Any promotional interest-free terms should be understood in full before committing.

Who Is Eligible for Dental Implant Finance?

Eligibility for dental finance depends on a number of factors assessed by the lending provider. While criteria can vary between lenders, the following are typically considered:

  • Age — applicants are usually required to be 18 or over
  • UK residency — most lenders require applicants to be UK residents with a valid UK address
  • Credit history — a credit check is carried out as part of the application process
  • Affordability — lenders assess whether the proposed repayments are manageable based on your income and outgoings

It is important to be aware that approval cannot be guaranteed in advance. Each application is assessed individually by the finance provider, and outcomes depend on personal financial circumstances at the time of application.

If finance is not approved, your dental practice can discuss alternative ways to manage treatment costs, such as phased treatment plans or prioritising the most clinically important work first.

Is Financing Dental Implants a Good Idea?

Whether finance is the right choice depends entirely on your individual circumstances. There is no one-size-fits-all answer, and it is worth weighing up the considerations carefully.

Paying Upfront vs Monthly Instalments

  • Paying in full avoids any interest charges and means no ongoing monthly commitment
  • Monthly payments allow treatment to proceed sooner without requiring the full amount upfront
  • Interest-bearing plans increase the total cost but reduce the monthly financial impact

Personal Budgeting Considerations

Before applying for finance, it is sensible to review your monthly budget and consider whether the repayments are sustainable over the full term. Dental implants are a long-term investment in your oral health, and the decision to finance should be made with the same care as any other financial commitment.

Dental implants can help preserve jawbone structure, protect neighbouring teeth and restore chewing function — benefits that contribute to long-term oral health. For some patients, the long-term value of treatment may justify spreading the cost, while others may prefer to save and pay in full.

What Is Included in the Cost of Dental Implants?

Understanding what is included in a dental implant quotation helps you compare options fairly and avoid unexpected charges. A comprehensive treatment plan should clearly outline all stages and associated costs.

Typical Inclusions

  • Initial consultation and clinical assessment — including examination and discussion of treatment options
  • Diagnostic imaging — such as X-rays or CBCT scans to assess bone quality and plan implant positioning
  • Surgical placement of the implant — the procedure to place the titanium implant into the jawbone
  • Abutment and final restoration — the connector piece and the visible crown, bridge or denture
  • Post-operative reviews — follow-up appointments to monitor healing and ensure satisfactory integration

Some quotations may not include preparatory treatments such as bone grafting, tooth extractions or treatment of gum disease. Always ask your dental practice to confirm exactly what is and is not included in the quoted price so that you can plan accordingly.

How to Plan for Dental Implant Treatment in 2026

Planning ahead is one of the most effective ways to manage the financial and practical aspects of dental implant treatment. Here are some steps to consider:

1. Book a Consultation

The first step is to arrange a dental check-up in London or an initial implant consultation. During this appointment, the dentist will examine your mouth, discuss your goals and explain whether implants are likely to be suitable for your situation.

2. Receive a Written Treatment Plan

Following your assessment, you should receive a detailed written treatment plan. This document outlines the proposed treatment stages, the estimated timeline and the costs involved. It provides a clear basis for making an informed decision.

3. Review Finance Options

If you wish to explore finance, your dental practice can provide information about the lending partners they work with and the types of plans that may be available. You may be given a finance illustration showing the monthly repayment amount, the interest rate (if applicable) and the total amount repayable.

4. Take Time to Consider

There is no obligation to proceed immediately. A reputable dental practice will encourage you to take the time you need to review your treatment plan, compare options and make a decision that feels right for you. If you have questions at any stage, your dental team should be happy to address them.

Dental Implants on Finance in London
